Blue Letter Bible study tools make reading, searching and studying the Bible easy and rewarding.

passages.title: 2 Chron. 20:1–30
passages.text: These verses describe a victory over Judah’s enemies in which God acts for his people. Faith in God and obedience to his prophets (v. 20 ) was the nation’s surest defense against their hostile neighbors (compare Ezra 4 ; Nehemiah 4 ).

passages.title: 2 Chron. 20:1–2
passages.text: **After this**. The invasion followed Jehoshaphat’s religious and judicial reforms (ch. 19 ), and so it was not a case of divine punishment (see 12:2 ). Instead it was an opportunity to exercise faith (compare note on 32:1–8 ). **great multitude**. Judah was apparently outnumbered by the coalition.

passages.title: 2 Chron. 20:3–4
passages.text: The **fast** expressed the special intensity of the people’s prayer (see Judg. 20:26 ; Ezra 8:21–23 ).

passages.title: 2 Chron. 20:14–19
passages.text: The people must **go down against** the enemy, but as prayerful observers, not as combatants. Verse 17 is based very closely on Ex. 14:13–14 .

passages.title: 2 Chron. 20:20–23
passages.text: The **wilderness of Tekoa** is about 12 miles (19 km) south of Jerusalem. Jehoshaphat’s call to faith is based on Isa. 7:9 . **Believe** here means the active and obedient trust that God rewards (see Heb. 11:6 ), acting on the revealed word of **his prophets**, including Jahaziel. **Ambush** may mean either angelic agents (see 2 Chron. 32:21 ) or men (see Judg. 9:25 ), in which case suspicions among the coalition forces lead to panic and their own destruction ( 2 Chron. 20:23 ; see 1 Sam. 14:20 ).

passages.title: 2 Chron. 20:24–30
passages.text: **Beracah** means “blessing.” The return to Jerusalem takes the form of a triumphal procession, which ends appropriately in the temple, where the people first sought God’s deliverance (v. 5 ).

passages.title: 2 Chron. 20:31–34
passages.text: **The high places, however, were not taken away**. Some have claimed that this contradicts 17:6 , which says that Jehoshaphat “took the high places . . . out of Judah.” Both statements can be true if 17:6 refers to Jehoshaphat’s official actions and 20:33 indicates that the people were not committed to Jehoshaphat’s reforms (see 1 Kings 22:43 ).

passages.title: 2 Chron. 20:35–37
passages.text: Jehoshaphat repeats his error of making an alliance (this time, a business agreement) with the Israelite king, Ahab’s son **Ahaziah**.
